summary: A standalone, lighter roll-and-write-style spinoff of Rajas of the Ganges that keeps the same race-to-intersect-money-and-fame idea but strips it down to shared dice and pencil-and-paper-style province building. It plays faster and simpler than the original, aimed at a broader, more casual audience.
praised: Faster, more accessible than the original
Keeps the clever crossing-tracks win condition
Good for introducing non-gamers to the family
criticised: Less depth than the base game
Feels like a simplified reskin rather than its own thing

interaction.kind: shared dice drafting, mostly parallel play
interaction.detail: Players draft from a shared pool of rolled dice each round but then develop their own paper province independently; interaction is limited to competing over which dice to take.

scoring.why: As in the original, the game ends the moment a player's fame and money markers meet
scoring.how_you_win: You win by developing your province efficiently enough that your fame and wealth trackers converge before anyone else's.

_name: Rajas of the Ganges: The Dice Charmers
